entities.summary: Bronislava of Poland was a Polish nun of the Premonstratensian Order who played a crucial role in the medieval Catholic Church. Born in the 12th century, she was dedicated to her faith and spent her life serving the poor and the sick. Bronislava was beatified in 1259 and her legacy continues to inspire religious orders and charities today. The Premonstratensian Order, to which she belonged, was founded in 1120 by St. Norbert, and Bronislava's dedication to her faith and service exemplified the Order's values of humility, obedience, and compassion. Bronislava's story serves as a testament to the enduring power of faith and service in shaping the course of human history.
